title: Man. Post. Cap. IX: GAR — imputing does not make one to have sinned; judicial declaration of reus
pass_a_gloss: Imputation does not make someone to have sinned; it presupposes that he sinned, in himself or in another. It is God's judicial act declaring him guilty and penalty-worthy for sin.
pass_b_english: God, by imputing sin to someone, does not make him to have sinned, but supposes him to have sinned, whether in himself or in another. For the imputation of sin is a judicial act of God, by which he declares someone to be guilty and worthy of penalty on account of sin, as was said from the beginning.
source_text: Deus imputando peccatum alicui, non facit ut peccaverit, sed supponit eum peccavisse, sive in se, sive in alio. Est enim imputatio peccati actus Dei iudicialis, quo declarat aliquem esse reum & dignum poena ob peccatum, ut ab initio dictum.
